q: מה מהבאים נכון לגבי תופעות לואי של טיפול באופיואידים בכאב כרוני בזקנים?
o: עצירות היא תופעת לוואי שמתפתחת לה סבילות ( TOLERANCE ) עם הזמן
עקב תופעות הלוואי אסור לעבור מינון מקסימלי של אופיואידים (CEILING EFFECT)
PSEUDOADDICTION היא תופעת לוואי המתבטאת בצריכה מופרזת של תרופה משנית לגורמים לא אורגניים
בהפסקה פתאומית של הטיפול יכולים להיות סימני גמילה
explanation:
**Physical dependence is not addiction**: opioid agonists can cause withdrawal when stopped (Hazzard 8e, p. 326). Constipation needs preventive treatment and monitoring; one should not wait on the assumption that it will necessarily disappear with continued use (p. 1075).

**A. Tolerance to constipation develops with time.** Wrong, tolerance to constipating effects may never occur, so time cannot be relied on to resolve constipation. The geriatric source recommends starting laxatives with opioids (Hazzard, p. 1075; AAPM/APS/ASAM consensus, 2001, p. 3).
**B. Adverse effects impose a maximum opioid dose, a ceiling effect.** Wrong, pure opioid agonists do not share a uniform pharmacologic dose ceiling in the sense proposed; clinical escalation remains limited by safety and adverse effects. This does not authorize unlimited dosing (AAPM/APS/ASAM, p. 3).
**C. Pseudoaddiction means excessive drug use caused by nonorganic factors.** Wrong, the historical term described drug-seeking attributed to undertreated pain, not use caused by nonorganic factors. Its validity as a distinct diagnosis was not established in the literature review, so it should not justify automatic opioid escalation (Greene and Chambers, 2015, concluding discussion; AAPM/APS/ASAM, p. 3).
**D. Abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal.** Correct, opioid agonists can cause physical dependence, so abruptly stopping sustained treatment may cause withdrawal; withdrawal alone does not prove addiction (Hazzard, p. 326).

Eighth-edition verification: Opioid agonists can cause physical dependence and withdrawal when stopped, supporting the withdrawal option. The discussion of buprenorphine's ceiling on respiratory depression must not be generalized to a uniform dose ceiling for all opioids (Hazzard 8e, p. 326).
Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 326, 1075; AAPM/APS/ASAM. Definitions Related to the Use of Opioids for the Treatment of Pain. 2001, p. 3, https://www.naabt.org/documents/APS_consensus_document.pdf; Greene MS, Chambers RA. Pseudoaddiction: Fact or Fiction? Curr Addict Rep. 2015;2:310-317, concluding discussion, doi:10.1007/s40429-015-0074-7.

explanationSource.status: Unsupported specific withdrawal-symptom list removed; page-supported dependence statement retained.

q: בן 88, סובל מדמנציה מתקדמת והוגדר כחולה נוטה למות על רקע מחלה זו. לאחרונה הוא אוכל מעט והצוות במחלקה הסיעודית שבה מטופל העלה אפשרות של "הזנת צינור". הוא לא השאיר הנחיות מקדימות או ייפוי כוח רפואי. מה האפשרויות החוקיות במצב זה (לפי המלצות ועד המותב)?
o: הארכת חיים מלאכותית בחולה נוטה למות הינה מנוגדת עקרונית לחוק ולכן לא מומלץ להאכיל בזונדה או PEG
הדרך המועדפת להאכלה של חולים עם דמנציה סופנית הינה ב- PEG
בחולה דמנציה המוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות מותר להמשיך הזנה פומית (COMFORT FEEDING ) ובמידת הצורך תוספת עירוי נוזלים
כדאי לדחות את התקנת ה PEG כמה שאפשר ולהשתמש בינתיים בזונדה, שכן פרוצדורת החדרת ה PEG הינה מורכבת
explanation:
התשובה הרשמית היא ג׳.

לפי המלצות המותב (עמ׳ 4–5), דרך הפה היא הדרך המועדפת למתן מזון ונוזלים; אם אינה מספקת, יש לשקול דרך חלופית לפי המצב הרפואי והוריות־הנגד של החולה המסוים.

**א. הארכת חיים מלאכותית בחולה נוטה למות הינה מנוגדת עקרונית לחוק ולכן לא מומלץ להאכיל בזונדה או PEG.** שגויה, אין איסור עקרוני כזה. ההמלצות מחייבות מזון ונוזלים גם באמצעים מלאכותיים בהיעדר הוריית נגד רפואית ברורה וספציפית בחולה המסוים (עמ׳ 5).
**ב. הדרך המועדפת להאכלה של חולים עם דמנציה סופנית הינה ב- PEG.** שגויה, העדיפות הראשונית היא להזנה דרך הפה. בחירת דרך חלופית נעשית לפי המצב הרפואי והיכולת להאכיל, ולכן אין המלצה אוטומטית ל-PEG לכל חולה (עמ׳ 5 עד 6).
**ג. בחולה דמנציה המוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות מותר להמשיך הזנה פומית (COMFORT FEEDING ) ובמידת הצורך תוספת עירוי נוזלים.** נכונה, זו התשובה הרשמית. ההמלצות מעדיפות מתן מזון ונוזלים דרך הפה, ואם אינו מספיק מחייבות לשקול דרך חלופית לפי צורכי החולה; עירוי הוא אחת האפשרויות, ולא פטור מהערכת ההזנה (עמ׳ 4 עד 6).
**ד. כדאי לדחות את התקנת ה PEG כמה שאפשר ולהשתמש בינתיים בזונדה, שכן פרוצדורת החדרת ה PEG הינה מורכבת.** שגויה, אין להחליף PEG בזונדה באופן קבוע בשל טענה כללית על מורכבות הפעולה. ההמלצות מציינות אי נוחות וסיבוכים של זונדה; דחייה קצרה של ההחלטה אפשרית לשם בירור רפואי תוך שמירת ההידרציה (עמ׳ 6).

**נקודת המפתח:** יש לתעד את ההחלטה ואת נימוקיה; ההמלצות אינן איסור גורף על הזנה מלאכותית (המלצות המותב, עמ׳ 5).

מקור: המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 4, 5, 6.
ref: המלצות ועד המותב — חוק החולה הנוטה למות

q: Why can a serious infection in a frail older adult present without reaching the conventional fever threshold?
o: A higher baseline temperature and an exaggerated temperature rise
A lower baseline temperature and a blunted temperature rise
A higher baseline temperature and a blunted temperature rise
A lower baseline temperature and an exaggerated temperature rise
explanation:
**Lower baseline temperature and a blunted inflammatory temperature response** make the conventional fever threshold less likely to be reached in older adults. Hazzard describes this combination as a reason infection can be recognized and treated late, particularly in frail older adults (p. 1669). "the combination of lower basal temperature and a blunted response makes it less likely that an older adult will reach the definition of fever" (p. 1669).

**A. A higher baseline temperature and an exaggerated temperature rise.** Wrong, the source describes a lower baseline and a dampened response, rather than either of these proposed increases (p. 1669).
**B. A lower baseline temperature and a blunted temperature rise.** Correct, both components match the source’s explanation for failing to reach the conventional fever threshold (p. 1669).
**C. A higher baseline temperature and a blunted temperature rise.** Wrong, the blunted response fits, but the source describes baseline temperature as lower rather than higher (p. 1669).
**D. A lower baseline temperature and an exaggerated temperature rise.** Wrong, the lower baseline fits, but inflammatory temperature increases are dampened rather than exaggerated (p. 1669).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1669.
ref: Hazzard Ch 104 — INFECTION AND APPROPRIATE ANTIMICROBIAL SELECTION

כל אדם מעל גיל 80

q: An older postoperative patient is at risk for venous thromboembolism, but bleeding risk is high and pharmacologic prophylaxis is currently contraindicated. Which approach is described in Hazzard?
o: Use intermittent pneumatic compression to reduce venous stasis.
Use reduced-dose heparin despite the established contraindication.
Observe without compression because the bleeding risk is high.
Defer prophylaxis until therapeutic anticoagulation becomes possible.
explanation:
**Mechanical prophylaxis** reduces venous stasis without requiring pharmacologic prophylaxis (p. 1522). Hazzard describes its use “as a stand alone method when bleeding risk is high and pharmacologic prophylaxis is contraindicated” (p. 1522). This matches the limitation established in the stem.

**A. Use intermittent pneumatic compression to reduce venous stasis.** Correct, intermittent pneumatic compression is a listed mechanical approach to minimizing venous stasis when pharmacologic prophylaxis is contraindicated (p. 1522).
**B. Use reduced-dose heparin despite the established contraindication.** Wrong, reducing a heparin dose does not follow the premise that pharmacologic prophylaxis is contraindicated; the source provides a mechanical alternative (p. 1522).
**C. Observe without compression because the bleeding risk is high.** Wrong, high bleeding risk is the situation in which the source describes standalone mechanical prophylaxis, rather than omission of compression (p. 1522).
**D. Defer prophylaxis until therapeutic anticoagulation becomes possible.** Wrong, the source describes a prophylactic mechanical option during the contraindication, so prophylaxis need not be deferred until therapeutic anticoagulation is possible (p. 1522).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1522.

q: After urgent problems have been treated, an older adult with periodontal disease needs a plan for the extent of dental treatment and tooth preservation. What should guide that plan?
o: The patient's chronological age as the basis for treatment
The patient's age group compared with younger adults
The average life expectancy for the patient's age and sex
The patient's health and function after oral and systemic assessment
explanation:
**Periodontal treatment planning** requires evaluation of oral and systemic factors. Hazzard identifies the person's health and functional status, rather than age itself, as the basis for determining treatment extent (p. 457). "The health and functional status of a person, rather than age per se, should determine the extent of periodontal treatment." (p. 457).

**A. The patient's chronological age as the basis for treatment.** Wrong, chronological age does not provide the individual health and functional assessment specified by the source (p. 457).
**B. The patient's age group compared with younger adults.** Wrong, comparison with an age group substitutes age for the individual oral and systemic assessment (p. 457).
**C. The average life expectancy for the patient's age and sex.** Wrong, an age-and-sex population average does not establish this person's health, function, or oral treatment needs (p. 457).
**D. The patient's health and function after oral and systemic assessment.** Correct, this combines the individual health and functional assessment with evaluation of oral and systemic factors (p. 457).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 457.

q: An 80-year-old woman in assisted living has moderate macular degeneration with visual acuity 20/200 and heart failure with ejection fraction 35%. She has stopped attending bingo, misses meals, and stays in bed. She takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Potassium is 3.2 and creatinine 1.4, compared with a baseline of 1.0. Alongside assessment of these medical findings, which environmental plan follows Hazzard's low-vision recommendations?
o: Improve lighting and contrast in activity areas and provide large-print bingo cards
Reduce contrast between bingo cards and background and provide smaller printed characters
Increase window glare in activity areas and place patterned backgrounds behind bingo cards
Dim task lighting in activity areas and reduce the size of printed signs
explanation:
**Visual accessibility** can be improved with appropriate lighting, contrast, and larger print. Hazzard emphasizes providing adequate light while limiting glare and reducing busy backgrounds; this is a targeted rehabilitation plan, not a claim that it resolves the other clinical findings (p. 482). "The challenge is to get enough light without creating glare, which can be disabling." (p. 482)

**A. Improve lighting and contrast in activity areas and provide large-print bingo cards.** Correct, the plan follows the listed strategies for reduced detailed vision: larger print, improved lighting, and stronger object-background contrast (p. 482).
**B. Reduce contrast between bingo cards and background and provide smaller printed characters.** Wrong, reduced contrast and smaller print work against the recommendations to increase contrast and enlarge material for loss of detailed vision (p. 482).
**C. Increase window glare in activity areas and place patterned backgrounds behind bingo cards.** Wrong, glare can be disabling, and the table recommends eliminating busy backgrounds rather than adding them (p. 482).
**D. Dim task lighting in activity areas and reduce the size of printed signs.** Wrong, dimming task lighting and shrinking signs oppose the recommended lighting and size adaptations for this visual problem (p. 482).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 482.
ref: Hazzard Ch 33 — LOW VISION: ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION

q: A 77-year-old man with diabetes is preparing for elective surgery. Why does Hazzard emphasize perioperative glucose monitoring and control?
o: Stress hyperglycemia may reduce the risk of infection
Anesthesia may correct the underlying glucose-regulation disorder
Stress hyperglycemia may increase the risk of infection
Glucose dysregulation may replace the need for infection surveillance
explanation:
**Impaired glucose regulation** and stress hyperglycemia are common perioperative concerns in older adults and may increase infection risk. The chapter therefore links glucose monitoring and control to potentially important benefits (p. 376): "careful monitoring to control blood sugars perioperatively may have important benefits."

**A. Stress hyperglycemia may reduce the risk of infection.** Wrong, the passage identifies a possible increase, rather than reduction, in infection risk with stress hyperglycemia (p. 376).
**B. Anesthesia may correct the underlying glucose-regulation disorder.** Wrong, the passage calls for monitoring and control because dysregulation remains a concern around surgery; it does not describe anesthesia as its correction (p. 376).
**C. Stress hyperglycemia may increase the risk of infection.** Correct, this is the risk relationship that the chapter gives as the reason for careful monitoring and control (p. 376).
**D. Glucose dysregulation may replace the need for infection surveillance.** Wrong, the source identifies infection risk as a concern requiring attention, not as something replaced by glucose dysregulation (p. 376).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 376.
ref: Hazzard Ch 27 — PERIOPERATIVE CARE: EVALUATION AND MANAGEMENT

q: A patient with delirium has several possible precipitants, including a medication change, an electrolyte disturbance, and acute illness. How should treatment address these factors?
o: Treat the relevant medication, metabolic, and medical contributors together
Correct the prominent laboratory result and defer further causal assessment
Suppress agitation first and defer treatment of the acute illness
Attribute the episode to dementia and defer investigation of new triggers
explanation:
**Delirium is usually multifactorial**: baseline vulnerability interacts with precipitating insults. Correcting one abnormality may not resolve the syndrome, so treatment needs to address the relevant contributors together (p. 881). "addressing many or all of the predisposing and precipitating factors for delirium is often required before the delirium symptoms will improve." (p. 881).

**A. Treat the relevant medication, metabolic, and medical contributors together.** Correct, it matches the source approach to cumulative contributors rather than assuming that correcting one finding is sufficient (p. 881).
**B. Correct the prominent laboratory result and defer further causal assessment.** Wrong, a prominent laboratory finding does not exclude other contributors; treatment of one factor alone often fails to resolve delirium (p. 881).
**C. Suppress agitation first and defer treatment of the acute illness.** Wrong, suppressing agitation does not address the acute illness identified as a possible precipitant; the source calls for treating relevant contributors (p. 881).
**D. Attribute the episode to dementia and defer investigation of new triggers.** Wrong, dementia increases vulnerability and does not remove the need to identify and address new precipitating insults (p. 881).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 881.

q: An 84-year-old woman with epilepsy, cognitive impairment, and medical comorbidities needs an antiseizure medication. Which principle should guide selection according to Hazzard?
o: Favor a sedating drug and give less weight to drug interactions
Favor a drug with few adverse effects and fewer drug interactions
Choose by chronological age and give less weight to kidney function
Choose a usual dose and give less weight to dizziness during treatment
explanation:
**Antiseizure drug selection** in older adults must account for adverse effects, medical comorbidities, and drug interactions. Cognitive dysfunction and dizziness are relevant adverse effects, and impaired kidney or liver function may alter drug levels (p. 994). "Given these concerns, ideal drugs should have minimal side effects and reduced chances for drug–drug interactions." (p. 994).

**A. Favor a sedating drug and give less weight to drug interactions.** Wrong, the source emphasizes minimizing adverse effects and interactions, not prioritizing sedation while discounting interactions (p. 994).
**B. Favor a drug with few adverse effects and fewer drug interactions.** Correct, this reflects the stated goal of minimal side effects and reduced interaction potential (p. 994).
**C. Choose by chronological age and give less weight to kidney function.** Wrong, renal function is specifically included among the comorbidities to consider, so age does not replace it (p. 994).
**D. Choose a usual dose and give less weight to dizziness during treatment.** Wrong, dizziness is a relevant adverse effect because it may increase fall risk and should not be discounted (p. 994).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 994.

q: A 79-year-old woman has recurrent near-syncope when rising from a chair after recently starting doxazosin 4 mg nightly for hypertension. Blood pressure is 158/78 supine and 122/68 after three minutes standing, with pulse rising from 68 to 74. Her daughter reports two falls this month and refusal to shower alone. She also takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Which medication-review approach follows the Beers recommendation for doxazosin used as an antihypertensive?
o: Stop doxazosin and reassess the antihypertensive regimen for an alternative
Reduce doxazosin and add midodrine while retaining it for hypertension
Stop hydrochlorothiazide and increase doxazosin for hypertension control
Add fludrocortisone and continue doxazosin for hypertension control
explanation:
**Doxazosin has a high risk of orthostatic hypotension and associated harms** in older adults. Beers advises avoiding its use as an antihypertensive because alternatives have a superior risk–benefit profile (p. 2058). "High risk of orthostatic hypotension and associated harms, especially in older adults" and "Avoid use as an antihypertensive." (p. 2058)

**A. Stop doxazosin and reassess the antihypertensive regimen for an alternative.** Correct, this applies the recommendation to remove doxazosin from its antihypertensive role and consider an alternative, rather than claiming a particular replacement dose is established by the source (p. 2058).
**B. Reduce doxazosin and add midodrine while retaining it for hypertension.** Wrong, adding a pressor while retaining doxazosin for hypertension does not implement the recommendation to avoid that antihypertensive use (p. 2058).
**C. Stop hydrochlorothiazide and increase doxazosin for hypertension control.** Wrong, increasing doxazosin continues the very antihypertensive exposure the source advises avoiding (p. 2058).
**D. Add fludrocortisone and continue doxazosin for hypertension control.** Wrong, adding fludrocortisone leaves doxazosin in its antihypertensive role and does not apply the stated recommendation (p. 2058).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2058.

q: בן 75, ללא מחלות רקע, נפל ושבר את הירך. עבר קיבוע ניתוחי. בבדיקות הדם בקבלה למחלקת שיקום: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים WBC 10e3/µL 9.8 4.0-11.0 HgB g/dL 8.5 13.2-17 גבר MCV fL 88 80-96 Plt 10e3/µL 187 150-450 Iron ng/mL 52 40-150 Transferrin mg/dL 250 220-400 Ferritin ng/mL 145 14-163 Vitamin B12 pg/mL 526 175-961 Folic Acid ng/mL 15 2.6-17.1 CREATININE mg/dL 1.0 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 26 5-25 מה הסיבה הכי סבירה לאנמיה אצל המטופל הזה?
o: אנמיה של Myelodysplastic Syndrome
אנמיה של מחלה כרונית
אנמיה פוסט ניתוחית
אנמיה של חסר ברזל
explanation:
**Postoperative anemia** is the most likely explanation after hip-fracture surgery, with peri-fracture and operative blood loss fitting the timing. This is a clinical inference, not a documented blood-loss volume (pp. 794, 1480). The supplied hemoglobin of 8.5 with normal MCV of 88 describes normocytic anemia, but does not by itself date its onset (p. 1480; interpretation of stem values).

**A. Myelodysplastic syndrome.** Wrong, no finding specifically favors MDS over the surgical context. Initial investigation precedes further hematological testing when indicated; normal counts in other lineages do not exclude MDS, which may present predominantly with anemia (pp. 1480, 1486).
**B. Anemia of chronic disease.** Wrong, no chronic disease is reported. This remains a differential diagnosis, but there are no positive findings favoring it over the recent surgery (p. 1480).
**C. Postoperative anemia.** Correct, the recent fracture and operation make perioperative blood loss the best contextual explanation. This is an inference from timing, not proof of the amount or onset of bleeding (pp. 794, 1480).
**D. Iron-deficiency anemia.** Wrong, the supplied iron indices are not low and do not provide positive evidence of deficiency. They should be interpreted as part of an anemia work-up; normal MCV alone does not exclude iron deficiency (p. 1480).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 794, 1480, 1486.

q: בת 85, מגיעה למיון לאחר שבר בצוואר הירך בליווי הבת שלה. אילו מהתסמינים הבאים יעוררו חשד גבוה להתעמרות נפשית במטופלת?
o: במעבר על גיליונות קודמים מסתבר שזו הפעם השלישית שמגיעה בעקבות שבר למיון
במעבר על תיק קופת החולים מסתבר שאינה רוכשת כמחצית מהתרופות הכרוניות שניתנו לה במרשם
בבדיקות המעבדה קריאטנין ו-BUN מוגברים באופן אקוטי
בשיחה עם המטופלת היא מסרבת לענות על שאלות כאשר הבת שלה נמצאת בחדר
explanation:
## חשד להתעמרות נפשית

סירוב לענות בנוכחות המלווה הוא **סימן מחשיד להתעמרות נפשית**, ולא הוכחה להתעמרות. הנוהל מונה פחד ואי־נוחות בנוכחות המטפל העיקרי וסירוב לדבר, ומנחה לבצע בדיקה ביחידות לפי שיקול דעת המטפל (נוהל משרד הבריאות, עמ׳ 6 ונספח 1 עמ׳ 1).

**א. במעבר על גיליונות קודמים מסתבר שזו הפעם השלישית שמגיעה בעקבות שבר למיון.** שגויה, פניות חוזרות בעקבות שברים מחייבות בירור, אך אינן כשלעצמן הסימן ההתנהגותי המכוון להתעמרות נפשית. הנוהל מפרט שברים לא מוסברים תחת פגיעה גופנית (נספח 1 עמ׳ 1; PDF עמ׳ 8).
**ב. במעבר על תיק קופת החולים מסתבר שאינה רוכשת כמחצית מהתרופות הכרוניות שניתנו לה במרשם.** שגויה, אי־רכישת תרופות מחייבת בירור הסיבה. הנוהל משייך אי־מילוי צרכים טיפוליים להזנחה; אין בממצא לבדו את הקשר ההתנהגותי לנוכחות המלווה (נספח 1 עמ׳ 2; PDF עמ׳ 9).
**ג. בבדיקות המעבדה קריאטנין ו-BUN מוגברים באופן אקוטי.** שגויה, ממצאי המעבדה מחייבים בירור רפואי. הנוהל מונה התייבשות בין סימני הזנחה; אין זה סימן ישיר להתעמרות נפשית כמו פחד או סירוב לדבר בנוכחות המטפל (נספח 1 עמ׳ 1–2; PDF עמ׳ 8–9; יישום למקרה).
**ד. בשיחה עם המטופלת היא מסרבת לענות על שאלות כאשר הבת שלה נמצאת בחדר.** נכונה, סירוב לדבר בנוכחות הבת תואם לסימנים ההתנהגותיים המפורטים בנוהל. יש לברר ביחידות, ולא להסיק מיד שהבת פוגעת בה (עמ׳ 6 ונספח 1 עמ׳ 1; PDF עמ׳ 6, 8).

מקור: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 6 ונספח 1 עמ׳ 1–2 (PDF עמ׳ 6, 8–9).

q: בן 75, ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית, אי-ספיקת כליות עם GFR של 45 מ"ל/דקה, אירוע של CVA בעבר. במעבדה – המוגלובין A1C – 8.9%. לאיזו מהתרופות הבאות לסוכרת יש פוטנציאל להביא לשינוי פרוגנוסטי למחלות הרקע?
o: משפחת GLP1 להורדת תסמיני אי-ספיקת לב
משפחת מעכבי SGLT2 לצורך הגנה כלייתית
METFORMIN כמניעה שניונית לשבץ
משפחת DPP4 למחלת לב איסכמית
explanation:
**Official answers:** GLP-1 agents to reduce heart-failure symptoms; SGLT2 inhibitors for renal protection (IMA, final answer key, June 2023 examination, question 68).
The drug table lists **slower CKD progression** among SGLT2-inhibitor benefits. Applying that benefit to diabetes with a GFR of 45 in the stem supports renal protection. It also lists cardiovascular-event reduction for some GLP-1 drugs, but that does not establish relief of heart-failure symptoms (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1577-1578, Table 99-11). The heart-failure-symptom option was added after appeals (IMA, June 2023, question 68).

**A. GLP-1 agents to reduce heart-failure symptoms.** Correct, accepted for official scoring. The table lists reduced cardiovascular events with some agents, but does not supply the claim of heart-failure symptom relief (p. 1577).
**B. SGLT2 inhibitors for renal protection.** Correct, also officially accepted and directly supported by the table's slower CKD progression, relevant to this patient's kidney disease (p. 1578).
**C. Metformin for secondary stroke prevention.** Wrong, the table lists likely reductions in microvascular and macrovascular events but does not establish specific secondary stroke prevention. A general vascular effect cannot replace that narrower claim (p. 1577).
**D. DPP-4 inhibitors for ischemic heart disease.** Wrong, the listed advantages concern glucose control and tolerability, not prognostic benefit in ischemic heart disease (p. 1577).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1577-1578, Table 99-11; the official key cited above.

q: איזה מסוגי השאלות הבאות נשאלות בשאלון AMT4?
o: שאלות על התמצאות
שאלות על תפקוד
שאלות על מצב בריאותי
שאלות על טיפול תרופתי
explanation:
**AMT4 (Abbreviated Mental Test 4)** is a brief cognitive screen with four **orientation** questions: age, date of birth, place (hospital or building) and current year. Within the 4AT figure, no mistakes score 0, one mistake scores 1, and two or more mistakes or inability to test score 2; interpret this together with the other 4AT components (Hazzard 8e, p. 211). The separate emergency-department dementia screening figure regards any AMT4 error as high risk for dementia (p. 212).

**A. Orientation questions.** Correct, age, date of birth, place and current year are the four listed items (pp. 211–212).
**B. Questions about function.** Wrong, none of the four items asks about functional ability (p. 211).
**C. Questions about health status.** Wrong, the four questions concern age, birthday, place and year, rather than health status (p. 212).
**D. Questions about medication.** Wrong, none of the four items asks about medications (p. 211).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 211–212, Figures 15-2 (continued) and 15-3.
referenceNote: Paper cites p.210; AMT4 is on p.211, the continuation of Figure 15-2.

q: איזה מהשינויים הפיזיולוגיים בהזדקנות הוא הנכון?
o: יש תגובה מופחתת לסטרס פיזי או נפשי ("Fight or Flight") ללא עליה משמעותית ברמות קורטיזול
יש תגובה מופחתת להתייבשות, עם שמירה של נפח הפלסמה בגוף וירידה ב-GFR
יש תגובה מופחתת לשינויים ברמת גלוקוז בדם, עם רגישות גבוהה לתסמיני היפרגליקמיה
יש תגובה מופחתת למלאות בשלפוחית השתן, עם ירידה ביכולת ההתכווצות של שריר ה- Detrusor
explanation:
Aging reduces the ability to sense and respond appropriately to bladder filling. The source also describes a mild reduction in **detrusor contractility** and greater susceptibility to decompensation with obstruction; these changes do not make retention or incontinence inevitable in every older person (pp. 581, 589).

**A. Reduced stress response without a significant cortisol rise.** Wrong, the table describes a prolonged increase in cortisol and sympathetic activity during stress (p. 581).
**B. Reduced response to dehydration with preserved plasma volume and reduced GFR.** Wrong, plasma volume decreases and water and sodium conservation are impaired; preserved volume is therefore inconsistent with the source, although reduced filtration is described (p. 581).
**C. Reduced response to glucose changes with high sensitivity to hyperglycemic symptoms.** Wrong, classical symptoms are less common in older adults; diabetes may remain undetected and present through complications or atypical symptoms (p. 1566).
**D. Reduced sensation of bladder filling with reduced detrusor contractility.** Correct, the source describes reduced sensing and response to filling as well as reduced contractility, supporting both parts of this option (pp. 581, 589).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 581, 589, 1566.
